claims.quote: Tay-Sachs disease is a severe neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the HEXA gene, which encodes the α-subunit of the β-hexosaminidase A (HexA) enzyme.
B4Galnt1 (ß-1,4-N-acetyl-galactosaminyltransferase 1) is involved in lipid biosynthesis in mice.
B4Galnt1 Deficiency Reverses Severe Neurological Symptoms in a Mouse Model of Tay-Sachs Disease.

Our findings suggest that knocking out B4Galnt1 to block GM2 ganglioside accumulation may reverse disease symptoms in the DKO mouse model, indicating a promising, safe target for substrate-reduction therapy via siRNA silencing.
